name: Kingdom of Arles
alt: Kingdom of Upper and Lower Burgundy

predecessors.name: Lower Burgundy
predecessors.text: Lower Burgundy: Provence, the Rhone valley and Vienne, ceded by Hugh of Italy in 933

predecessors.name: Upper Burgundy
predecessors.text: Rudolph II's Upper Burgundy: Franche-Comte, Savoy and western Switzerland, 171 cells of Cliopatria's shape inside the Arles shape

successors.name: County of Savoy
successors.text: Savoy, Aosta and the Valais as the count of Savoy held them; transferred from Burgundy to the Kingdom of Germany in 1361

successors.name: Dauphiné
successors.text: the Dauphine of Viennois, sold to the House of Valois in 1349

successors.name: Free County of Burgundy
successors.text: Franche-Comte, the imperial County of Burgundy

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the Vivarais (1306), Lyon (1312), the Dauphine (1349) and, from 1481, Provence

successors.name: Swiss Confederation
successors.text: the Swiss cantons in the old kingdom, 30 cells in 1384

ledger.x: 933: Rudolph II unites Upper and Lower Burgundy into one kingdom.
933: Hugh of Italy cedes Lower Burgundy to Rudolph II.
1006: Rudolph III cedes Basel to Henry II.
1032: Rudolph III dies without heirs and the kingdom passes to the Salian emperor Conrad II.
1246: Provence passes to Charles of Anjou.
1306: the Vivarais is recognised as French.
1312: Lyon passes to the French crown.
1349: the Dauphine is sold to the French crown.
1361: Charles IV transfers Savoy from the Kingdom of Burgundy to the Kingdom of Germany.
1384: the kingdom is a name only.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes the kingdom's frontier; the 1006 cession of Basel and the 1312 treaty for Lyon are the only dated boundary acts and are sharp only at those places.
